t: Constitutional monarchy keeps a hereditary head of state but binds the crown by law; in its parliamentary form the monarch reigns while elected ministers govern.
It took shape in England with the Bill of Rights 1689 and spread through 19th-century Europe, then to Japan, Siam and the self-governing dominions of the British Empire.
After two world wars swept away many thrones, the surviving monarchies of Europe almost all adopted the British model of a ceremonial crown and parliamentary government.
dyk: No British monarch has refused royal assent to a bill since 11 March 1708, when Queen Anne withheld it from the Scottish Militia Bill; the power has never been abolished but is widely thought to have lapsed.
ev: The Bill of Rights forbids the English crown to suspend laws, levy taxes or keep a peacetime army without Parliament
The Act of Settlement fixes a Protestant succession by statute, later bringing the House of Hanover to the throne
Queen Anne withholds assent from the Scottish Militia Bill, the last royal veto in Britain
Poland–Lithuania adopts the Constitution of 3 May, often called Europe’s first modern written constitution
Belgium’s constitution declares that all powers emanate from the nation; Leopold I swears to uphold it
Japan’s Meiji Constitution creates an Imperial Diet with an elected lower house under a sovereign emperor
Japan’s new constitution makes the emperor “the symbol of the State and of the unity of the people”
Spain’s constitution restores parliamentary monarchy under Juan Carlos I after Franco’s dictatorship

f.power: Shared under a constitution: in most, an elected parliament and a cabinet answerable to it govern while the monarch acts on ministers’ advice; in some the monarch keeps real executive powers
f.legitimacy: Hereditary right bound by law: the crown’s authority rests on a constitution, statutes and conventions, the government’s on the consent of voters expressed through parliament
f.chosen: The monarch by hereditary succession regulated by law, such as the Act of Settlement 1701; ministers through parliamentary elections and the confidence of the legislature
f.examples: Kingdom of Great Britain (1707–1800), Kingdom of Norway under the Constitution of 1814, Kingdom of Belgium under the Constitution of 1831, German Empire (1871–1918), Empire of Japan under the Meiji Constitution, Kingdom of Spain since 1978
